name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Mechanisms of respiration across animal taxa

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding respiratory mechanisms across different animal groups and the human conducting airway:

Statement I: Lower invertebrates like sponges, coelenterates, and flatworms exchange \(O_2\) with \(CO_2\) by simple diffusion over their entire body surface.
Statement II: Earthworms utilize their moist cuticle for cutaneous gas exchange, whereas insects possess a branching network of tracheal tubes.
Statement III: Specialized vascularized structures called gills are used by most aquatic arthropods and molluscs, whereas lungs are used by terrestrial vertebrates.
Statement IV: The conducting part of the human respiratory tract clears foreign particles, humidifies inhaled atmospheric air, and brings it to body temperature.
Statement V: The respiratory exchange part of the human respiratory system consists exclusively of the trachea and terminal bronchioles, completely lacking alveoli.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

विभिन्न प्राणी समूहों में श्वसन क्रियाविधि और मानव संवहनीय वायुमार्ग के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: स्पंज, सीलेन्टरेट और चपटे कृमि जैसे निम्न अकशेरुकी अपनी संपूर्ण शारीरिक सतह से सरल विसरण द्वारा \(O_2\) और \(CO_2\) का आदान-प्रदान करते हैं।
कथन II: केंचुए त्वचीय गैस विनिमय के लिए अपनी नम उपत्वचा (क्यूटिकल) का उपयोग करते हैं, जबकि कीटों में श्वासनली नलिकाओं (ट्रेकियल ट्यूब्स) का शाखित जाल होता है।
कथन III: अधिकांश जलीय आर्थ्रोपोड और मोलस्क विशिष्ट संवहनीकृत संरचनाओं जिन्हें क्लोम (गिल्स) कहते हैं का उपयोग करते हैं, जबकि स्थलीय कशेरुकी फेफड़ों का उपयोग करते हैं।
कथन IV: मानव श्वसन तंत्र का संवहन भाग अंतःश्वसित वायु को धूल कणों से मुक्त करता है, नम बनाता है तथा शरीर के तापमान पर लाता है।
कथन V: मानव श्वसन तंत्र का श्वसन विनिमय भाग केवल श्वासनली और अंतस्थ श्वसनिकाओं से बना होता है, जिसमें कूपिकाओं का पूर्णतः अभाव होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding lower invertebrates
Lower invertebrates such as sponges, cnidarians (coelenterates), and flatworms lack specialized respiratory organs. Because all living cells reside in close proximity to the surrounding water, exchange of \(O_2\) and \(CO_2\) takes place by simple diffusion across their entire body surface. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding earthworms and insects
Earthworms respire cutaneously using their thin, moist cuticle, while insects possess an internal network of tracheal tubes that conduct atmospheric air directly to metabolizing cells. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding aquatic and terrestrial organs
Vascularized outgrowths called gills (branchial respiration) are adapted for underwater gas exchange in aquatic arthropods, molluscs, and fishes. In contrast, vascularized bags called lungs (pulmonary respiration) are used by terrestrial vertebrates, including reptiles, birds, and mammals. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding the conducting zone functions
The conducting portion extends from the external nostrils to the terminal bronchioles. It filters atmospheric air via mucus and cilia, humidifies the air stream, and thermally equilibrates incoming gas to internal body temperature. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding the respiratory exchange zone
The exchange (respiratory) part consists of the thin-walled alveoli and their alveolar ducts, where actual diffusion between blood and air takes place. The trachea and terminal bronchioles are strictly parts of the conducting zone, not the exchange zone. Hence, this claim is inaccurate.

Step 6: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The propositions concerning lower invertebrate diffusion, earthworm/insect anatomy, aquatic versus terrestrial organs, and conducting zone conditioning functions are all scientifically accurate, whereas the proposition misidentifying the exchange part is inaccurate.
Final Conceptual Answer: Only the propositions detailing simple diffusion in lower invertebrates, cuticle and tracheal adaptations, gills versus lungs, and conducting zone functions are correct.

चरण 1: निम्न अकशेरुकियों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
स्पंज, सीलेन्टरेट और चपटे कृमियों में विशेष श्वसन अंगों का अभाव होता है और संपूर्ण शारीरिक सतह से सरल विसरण द्वारा गैस विनिमय होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: केंचुओं और कीटों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
केंचुए अपनी नम क्यूटिकल से तथा कीट ट्रेकियल नलिकाओं के जाल द्वारा श्वसन करते हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: जलीय एवं स्थलीय श्वसन अंगों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
जलीय आर्थ्रोपोड, मोलस्क और मछलियां क्लोम (गिल्स) का उपयोग करती हैं, जबकि स्थलीय कशेरुकी फेफड़ों का उपयोग करते हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: संवहन भाग के कार्यों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
श्वसन मार्ग का संवहन भाग वायु को कूपिकाओं तक पहुंचाता है, धूल-कणों को साफ करता है, इसे नम बनाता है और शरीर के तापमान पर लाता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: श्वसन विनिमय भाग संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
गैस विनिमय भाग कूपिकाओं और उनकी नलिकाओं से बनता है, जहां गैसों का वास्तविक विसरण होता है। श्वासनली और अंतस्थ श्वसनिकाएं संवहन भाग के अंग हैं, विनिमय भाग के नहीं। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 6: निष्कर्ष और अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर
प्रथम चार अवधारणाएं पूर्णतः सही हैं, जबकि विनिमय भाग में कूपिकाओं का अभाव बताने वाली अवधारणा गलत है।
अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और चतुर्थ अवधारणाएं ही सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Thoracic cage architecture and ventilation mechanics

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the anatomy of the thoracic chamber and the mechanics of breathing:

Statement I: The thoracic chamber is formed dorsally by the vertebral column, ventrally by the sternum, laterally by the ribs, and inferiorly by the dome-shaped diaphragm.
Statement II: Any change in thoracic volume is directly reflected in pulmonary volume because humans cannot directly alter pulmonary volume independently.
Statement III: Contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis.
Statement IV: Contraction of external intercostal muscles lifts the ribs and sternum, causing an increase in thoracic volume in the dorso-ventral axis.
Statement V: Relaxation of the diaphragm causes it to flatten downward, resulting in an enormous increase in thoracic chamber volume.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

वक्षीय गुहा की शारीरिक संरचना और श्वसन की क्रियाविधि के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: वक्षीय गुहा पृष्ठ भाग में कशेरुक दंड, अधर भाग में उरोस्थि (स्टर्नम), पार्श्व में पसलियों और नीचे की ओर गुंबदाकार डायाफ्राम द्वारा निर्मित होती है।
कथन II: वक्षीय गुहा के आयतन में कोई भी परिवर्तन फुप्फुसी गुहा में सीधे प्रतिबिंबित होता है क्योंकि मनुष्य सीधे तौर पर फुप्फुसी आयतन को नहीं बदल सकते।
कथन III: डायाफ्राम का संकुचन वक्षीय गुहा के आयतन को अग्र-पश्च (एंटीरो-पोस्टीरियर) अक्ष में बढ़ा देता है।
कथन IV: बाह्य अंतरापर्शुक पेशियों का संकुचन पसलियों और उरोस्थि को ऊपर उठाता है, जिससे पृष्ठ-अधर (डोर्सो-वेंट्रल) अक्ष में वक्षीय आयतन में वृद्धि होती है।
कथन V: डायाफ्राम का शिथिलन (रिलैक्सेशन) इसे नीचे की ओर चपटा कर देता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप वक्षीय गुहा के आयतन में भारी वृद्धि होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding thoracic cavity boundaries
The thoracic chamber is an air-tight structural enclosure defined dorsally by the vertebral column, ventrally by the sternum, laterally by the rib cage, and bounded on its lower floor by the dome-shaped diaphragm. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding thoracic-pulmonary volume coupling
Because the lungs are enclosed within the pleural sac adhering to the thoracic wall and lack self-actuating skeletal muscle within their parenchymal walls, pulmonary volume cannot be actively controlled directly. Any volumetric alteration in the thoracic cavity is obligatorily transmitted to the pulmonary cavity. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding diaphragmatic contraction axis
Contraction of the diaphragmatic musculature flattens its dome downward, thereby increasing the dimension of the thoracic cavity along its longitudinal or antero-posterior axis. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding external intercostal muscle action
Contraction of the external intercostal muscles rotates and elevates the ribs and moves the sternum outward, which expands the thoracic cavity in the dorso-ventral axis. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding diaphragmatic relaxation
Relaxation of the diaphragm allows abdominal pressure and elastic recoil to push it back upward into its natural dome shape, which decreases the thoracic volume. Contraction flattens the diaphragm, not relaxation. Hence, this claim is inaccurate.

Step 6: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The structural boundaries of the thorax, the obligatory volume coupling, and the directional muscle actions expanding the thoracic dimensions during inspiration are all correct, whereas diaphragmatic relaxation decreases volume rather than increasing it.
Final Conceptual Answer: Only the propositions describing thoracic cage boundaries, mechanical thoracic-pulmonary coupling, antero-posterior expansion by the diaphragm, and dorso-ventral expansion by external intercostals are correct.

चरण 1: वक्षीय गुहा की सीमाओं संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
वक्षीय कक्ष पृष्ठ भाग में कशेरुक दंड, अधर भाग में उरोस्थि, पार्श्व में पसलियों तथा निचले तल पर डायाफ्राम द्वारा निर्मित एक वायुरुद्ध कक्ष है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: वक्षीय एवं फुप्फुसी आयतन के संबंध संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
फेफड़े स्वयं अपनी पेशियों द्वारा प्रसारित नहीं हो सकते; अतः वक्षीय गुहा का कोई भी आयतन परिवर्तन फुप्फुसीय गुहा में सीधा परिलक्षित होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: डायाफ्राम संकुचन के अक्ष संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
डायाफ्राम के संकुचित होकर चपटा होने से अग्र-पश्च अक्ष में वक्षीय आयतन में वृद्धि होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: बाह्य अंतरापर्शुक पेशियों की क्रिया संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
बाह्य अंतरापर्शुक पेशियों के संकुचन से पसलियां और उरोस्थि ऊपर उठती हैं, जिससे पृष्ठ-अधर अक्ष में वक्षीय आयतन बढ़ता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: डायाफ्राम के शिथिलन संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
डायाफ्राम के शिथिल (रिलैक्स) होने पर यह पुनः ऊपर की ओर गुंबदाकार हो जाता है और वक्षीय आयतन घटता है। इसका चपटा होना संकुचन के दौरान होता है, शिथिलन में नहीं। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 6: निष्कर्ष और अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर
प्रथम चार अवधारणाएं शारीरिक और यांत्रिक दृष्टि से सही हैं, जबकि डायाफ्राम शिथिलन में आयतन वृद्धि का दावा गलत है।
अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और चतुर्थ अवधारणाएं ही सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Evaluation of respiratory volumes and capacities

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding respiratory volumes and clinical pulmonary capacities:

Statement I: Tidal Volume (TV) is approximately \(500\text{ mL}\), meaning a healthy man can inspire or expire approximately \(6000\text{ to }8000\text{ mL}\) of air per minute.
Statement II: Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV) averages \(2500\text{ mL}\) to \(3000\text{ mL}\).
Statement III: Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) averages \(1000\text{ mL}\) to \(1100\text{ mL}\), and Residual Volume (RV) averages \(1100\text{ mL}\) to \(1200\text{ mL}\).
Statement IV: Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal expiration and is calculated as \(ERV + RV\).
Statement V: Vital Capacity (VC) is mathematically determined by subtracting Tidal Volume from Residual Volume (\(RV - TV\)).

Which of the statements given above are correct?

श्वसन आयतनों और नैदानिक फुप्फुसीय क्षमताओं के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: ज्वारीय आयतन (TV) लगभग \(500\text{ mL}\) होता है, अर्थात एक स्वस्थ मनुष्य प्रति मिनट लगभग \(6000\) से \(8000\text{ mL}\) वायु अंतःश्वसित या निःश्वसित कर सकता है।
कथन II: अंतःश्वसन सुरक्षित आयतन (IRV) औसतन \(2500\text{ mL}\) से \(3000\text{ mL}\) होता है।
कथन III: निःश्वसन सुरक्षित आयतन (ERV) औसतन \(1000\text{ mL}\) से \(1100\text{ mL}\) तथा अवशिष्ट आयतन (RV) औसतन \(1100\text{ mL}\) से \(1200\text{ mL}\) होता है।
कथन IV: प्रकार्यात्मक अवशिष्ट क्षमता (FRC) सामान्य निःश्वसन के बाद फेफड़ों में बची रहने वाली वायु का आयतन है और इसकी गणना \(ERV + RV\) के रूप में की जाती है।
कथन V: जैव क्षमता (VC) की गणना गणितीय रूप से अवशिष्ट आयतन में से ज्वारीय आयतन को घटाकर (\(RV - TV\)) की जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding Tidal Volume
Tidal volume is the volume of gas moved per normal unforced breath (\(\approx 500\text{ mL}\)). With a normal respiratory rate of \(12\text{ to }16\text{ breaths/min}\), minute ventilation ranges between \(6000\text{ and }8000\text{ mL/min}\). Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding Inspiratory Reserve Volume
Inspiratory Reserve Volume is the maximum additional volume that can be inhaled forcibly above tidal volume and ranges between \(2500\text{ mL and }3000\text{ mL}\). Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding ERV and RV
Expiratory Reserve Volume averages \(1000\text{ to }1100\text{ mL}\), while Residual Volume (the air that cannot be expelled even by maximal effort) averages \(1100\text{ to }1200\text{ mL}\). Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding Functional Residual Capacity
Functional Residual Capacity represents the resting end-expiratory air volume remaining in the lungs following a normal, non-forced expiration. It equals \(ERV + RV\). Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding Vital Capacity calculation
Vital Capacity represents the maximum volume of air a person can breathe out after a forced inspiration (or breathe in after a forced expiration), formulated as \(VC = ERV + TV + IRV\). Subtracting \(TV\) from \(RV\) is physiologically erroneous. Hence, this claim is inaccurate.

Step 6: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The specific numerical ranges for TV, IRV, ERV, RV, and the summation formula for FRC are all valid, whereas the formula provided for Vital Capacity is invalid.
Final Conceptual Answer: Only the propositions defining Tidal Volume, Inspiratory Reserve Volume, Expiratory Reserve/Residual Volumes, and Functional Residual Capacity are correct.

चरण 1: ज्वारीय आयतन (TV) संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
सामान्य श्वसन में ज्वारीय आयतन \(500\text{ mL}\) और प्रति मिनट संवातन \(6000-8000\text{ mL}\) होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: अंतःश्वसन सुरक्षित आयतन (IRV) संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
बलपूर्वक अंतःश्वसित किया जा सकने वाला अतिरिक्त आयतन \(2500-3000\text{ mL}\) होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: ERV और RV संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
ERV का औसत मान \(1000-1100\text{ mL}\) तथा RV का मान \(1100-1200\text{ mL}\) होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: प्रकार्यात्मक अवशिष्ट क्षमता (FRC) संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
सामान्य निःश्वसन के बाद बची वायु FRC कहलाती है, जिसका मान \(ERV + RV\) होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: जैव क्षमता (VC) की गणना संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
जैव क्षमता अधिकतम बलपूर्वक ली या छोड़ी जा सकने वाली वायु होती है, जिसका सूत्र \(VC = ERV + TV + IRV\) होता है। \(RV - TV\) का कोई औचित्य नहीं है। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 6: निष्कर्ष और अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर
प्रथम चार अवधारणाएं पूर्णतः सही हैं, जबकि जैव क्षमता की परिभाषा व सूत्र गलत दिया गया है।
अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और चतुर्थ अवधारणाएं ही सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q04 - Diffusion barrier and partial pressure gradients

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding the respiratory diffusion membrane and partial pressure dynamics:

Statement I: The respiratory diffusion membrane is composed of three major layers: thin squamous epithelium of alveoli, endothelium of alveolar capillaries, and intervening basement substance.
Statement II: The total thickness of the respiratory diffusion membrane is much less than a millimetre.
Statement III: The solubility of \(CO_2\) in respiratory fluids is \(20\text{ to }25\) times higher than that of \(O_2\).
Statement IV: In the alveoli, partial pressures are \(pO_2 = 104\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(pCO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}\), whereas in incoming deoxygenated blood they are \(pO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(pCO_2 = 45\text{ mm Hg}\).
Statement V: In oxygenated blood leaving the pulmonary capillaries, \(pO_2\) is \(40\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(pCO_2\) is \(95\text{ mm Hg}\).

Which of the statements given above are correct?

श्वसन विसरण झिल्ली और आंशिक दाब गतिकी के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: श्वसन विसरण झिल्ली तीन मुख्य परतों से मिलकर बनी होती है: कूपिका की पतली शल्की उपकला, कूपिकीय केशिकाओं की अंतःकला और उनके बीच स्थित आधारीय पदार्थ।
कथन II: श्वसन विसरण झिल्ली की कुल मोटाई एक मिलीमीटर से बहुत कम होती है।
कथन III: श्वसन द्रवों में \(CO_2\) की विलेयता \(O_2\) की तुलना में \(20\) से \(25\) गुना अधिक होती है।
कथन IV: कूपिकाओं में आंशिक दाब \(pO_2 = 104\text{ mm Hg}\) तथा \(pCO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}\) होते हैं, जबकि आने वाले विऑक्सीकृत रक्त में \(pO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}\) तथा \(pCO_2 = 45\text{ mm Hg}\) होते हैं।
कथन V: फुप्फुसीय केशिकाओं से निकलने वाले ऑक्सीकृत रक्त में \(pO_2\) का मान \(40\text{ mm Hg}\) तथा \(pCO_2\) का मान \(95\text{ mm Hg}\) होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding diffusion membrane layers
The diffusion barrier between alveolar lumen and blood consists of three layers: (1) single-layered squamous epithelium of the alveolar wall, (2) single-layered endothelium of the pulmonary capillary, and (3) the thin intervening basement substance. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding diffusion membrane thickness
The total anatomical thickness of the tripartite diffusion membrane is microscopic (\(0.2\text{ to }0.5\ \mu\text{m}\)), which is vastly less than a single millimetre, enabling rapid diffusion. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding gas solubilities
Carbon dioxide possesses a Bunsen solubility coefficient that is 20 to 25 times greater than that of oxygen. Thus, across an equal partial pressure gradient, \(CO_2\) diffuses at a substantially greater rate than \(O_2\). Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding alveolar and venous partial pressures
In alveolar spaces, \(pO_2\) is \(104\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(pCO_2\) is \(40\text{ mm Hg}\). In deoxygenated venous blood entering the pulmonary capillaries, \(pO_2\) is \(40\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(pCO_2\) is \(45\text{ mm Hg}\), ensuring favourable downhill gradients for both gases. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding oxygenated blood values
Oxygenated blood leaving the pulmonary capillaries has a \(pO_2\) of \(95\text{ mm Hg}\) and a \(pCO_2\) of \(40\text{ mm Hg}\). Stating that \(pO_2\) is \(40\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(pCO_2\) is \(95\text{ mm Hg}\) completely inverts and misstates physiological blood gas values. Hence, this claim is inaccurate.

Step 6: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The histological organization of the diffusion barrier, its sub-millimetre thinness, the 20-25 fold higher solubility of carbon dioxide, and the baseline alveolar/venous partial pressure values are all correct, while the values for oxygenated blood are incorrect.
Final Conceptual Answer: Only the propositions describing the three diffusion membrane layers, sub-millimetre thickness, high carbon dioxide solubility, and alveolar/deoxygenated partial pressures are correct.

चरण 1: विसरण झिल्ली की परतों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
विसरण झिल्ली तीन स्तरों से बनी होती है: कूपिका की शल्की उपकला, केशिका की अंतःकला और उनके मध्य आधारीय पदार्थ। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: विसरण झिल्ली की मोटाई संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
विसरण झिल्ली की कुल मोटाई एक मिलीमीटर से बहुत कम होती है, जो तीव्र विसरण को सुगम बनाती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: गैसों की विलेयता संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
द्रवों में \(CO_2\) की विलेयता \(O_2\) की तुलना में \(20\) से \(25\) गुना अधिक होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: कूपिका एवं विऑक्सीकृत रक्त के आंशिक दाब संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
कूपिका में \(pO_2 = 104\text{ mm Hg}\), \(pCO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}\) तथा विऑक्सीकृत रक्त में \(pO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}\), \(pCO_2 = 45\text{ mm Hg}\) होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: ऑक्सीकृत रक्त के आंशिक दाब संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
ऑक्सीकृत रक्त में \(pO_2 = 95\text{ mm Hg}\) तथा \(pCO_2 = 40\text{ mm Hg}\) होता है। कथन में इन मानों को गलत और विपरीत दर्शाया गया है। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 6: निष्कर्ष और अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर
प्रथम चार अवधारणाएं पूर्णतः सत्य हैं, जबकि ऑक्सीकृत रक्त के आंशिक दाब संबंधी अवधारणा असत्य है।
अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और चतुर्थ अवधारणाएं ही सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Oxygen transport and dissociation curve kinetics

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding oxygen transport and the haemoglobin-oxygen dissociation curve:

Statement I: About \(97\%\) of oxygen is transported bound to haemoglobin in RBCs, while the remaining \(3\%\) is carried dissolved in plasma.
Statement II: Each haemoglobin molecule can bind reversibly with a maximum of four molecules of \(O_2\).
Statement III: A sigmoid curve is obtained when percentage saturation of haemoglobin with \(O_2\) is plotted against \(pO_2\).
Statement IV: In the alveoli, high \(pO_2\), low \(pCO_2\), lesser \(H^+\) concentration, and lower temperature favour the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
Statement V: Under normal physiological resting conditions, every \(100\text{ mL}\) of oxygenated blood delivers approximately \(50\text{ mL}\) of \(O_2\) to the tissues.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

ऑक्सीजन परिवहन और हीमोग्लोबिन-ऑक्सीजन वियोजन वक्र के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: लगभग \(97\%\) ऑक्सीजन का परिवहन RBCs में हीमोग्लोबिन से जुड़कर होता है, जबकि शेष \(3\%\) प्लाज्मा में घुलित अवस्था में ले जाई जाती है।
कथन II: प्रत्येक हीमोग्लोबिन अणु उत्क्रमणीय रूप से अधिकतम चार \(O_2\) अणुओं को बांध सकता है।
कथन III: जब \(pO_2\) के विरुद्ध हीमोग्लोबिन की \(O_2\) के साथ प्रतिशत संतृप्ति को आलेखित किया जाता है, तो एक सिग्मॉइड (एस-आकार का) वक्र प्राप्त होता है।
कथन IV: कूपिकाओं में उच्च \(pO_2\), निम्न \(pCO_2\), कम \(H^+\) सांद्रता तथा कम तापमान ऑक्सीहीमोग्लोबिन के निर्माण के अनुकूल कारक हैं।
कथन V: सामान्य विश्राम की शारीरिक परिस्थितियों में, प्रत्येक \(100\text{ mL}\) ऑक्सीकृत रक्त ऊतकों को लगभग \(50\text{ mL}\) \(O_2\) प्रदान करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding oxygen transport partitioning
Due to the low physical solubility of oxygen in plasma water, only \(3\%\) is carried in physical solution, whereas \(97\%\) is reversibly bound to the iron atoms of haemoglobin inside erythrocytes. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding haemoglobin stoichiometry
Haemoglobin is a tetrameric globular protein possessing four separate heme prosthetic rings. Each ferrous (\(Fe^{2+}\)) center reversibly coordinates one diatomic oxygen molecule, allowing one haemoglobin molecule to carry up to four \(O_2\) molecules. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding curve shape
Due to cooperative allosteric binding among the four subunits, oxygen binding exhibits positive cooperativity, generating a classic sigmoid (S-shaped) saturation curve across physiological oxygen partial pressures. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding alveolar association conditions
In pulmonary capillary beds, high \(pO_2\) (\(104\text{ mm Hg}\)), coupled with low \(pCO_2\) (\(40\text{ mm Hg}\)), lower \([H^+]\) (alkaline pH), and lower temperature, stabilizes the relaxed (R) quaternary state of haemoglobin, strongly favouring oxyhaemoglobin synthesis. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding resting oxygen delivery volume
Under basal resting conditions, \(100\text{ mL}\) of arterial blood transports approximately \(19.4\text{ to }20\text{ mL}\) of oxygen, of which roughly \(5\text{ mL}\) is unloaded at the tissues (venous return blood contains \(\approx 14.4\text{ to }15\text{ mL}\)). Claiming that \(50\text{ mL}\) is delivered per \(100\text{ mL}\) of blood is impossible. Hence, this claim is inaccurate.

Step 6: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The partitioning percentages, tetrameric stoichiometry, sigmoidal dissociation kinetics, and alveolar factors favouring loading are all correct, whereas resting tissue delivery is 5 mL per 100 mL of blood, not 50 mL.
Final Conceptual Answer: Only the propositions detailing oxygen transport fractions, four-molecule stoichiometry, sigmoidal saturation curve, and alveolar loading factors are correct.

चरण 1: ऑक्सीजन परिवहन के वितरण संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
लगभग \(97\%\) ऑक्सीजन का परिवहन लाल रक्त कणिकाओं में हीमोग्लोबिन से जुड़कर होता है और \(3\%\) प्लाज्मा में घुलकर परिवहित होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: हीमोग्लोबिन की बंधन क्षमता संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
प्रत्येक हीमोग्लोबिन अणु में 4 हीम समूह होते हैं, जो अधिकतम 4 ऑक्सीजन अणुओं को उत्क्रमणीय रूप से बांध सकते हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: वक्र की प्रकृति संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
सहकारी बंधन के कारण हीमोग्लोबिन की प्रतिशत संतृप्ति और \(pO_2\) के मध्य आलेखित वक्र सिग्मॉइड (सिग्माभ) होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: कूपिकीय परिस्थितियों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
कूपिकाओं में उच्च \(pO_2\), निम्न \(pCO_2\), कम \(H^+\) सांद्रता तथा कम तापमान ऑक्सीहीमोग्लोबिन निर्माण के लिए अनुकूल होते हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: ऊतकों को ऑक्सीजन आपूर्ति संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
सामान्य विश्राम की अवस्था में, प्रत्येक \(100\text{ mL}\) ऑक्सीकृत रक्त ऊतकों को केवल लगभग \(5\text{ mL}\) ऑक्सीजन प्रदान करता है, \(50\text{ mL}\) नहीं। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 6: निष्कर्ष और अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर
प्रथम चार अवधारणाएं वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि ऊतकों को \(50\text{ mL}\) ऑक्सीजन आपूर्ति का दावा असत्य है।
अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और चतुर्थ अवधारणाएं ही सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q06 - Carbon dioxide transport and neural regulation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements regarding carbon dioxide transport mechanisms and the neural regulation of respiration:

Statement I: Nearly \(20\text{ to }25\%\) of \(CO_2\) is carried as carbamino-haemoglobin, and approximately \(70\%\) is carried as bicarbonate ions.
Statement II: Red blood cells contain a very high concentration of carbonic anhydrase, whereas blood plasma contains only minute quantities of this enzyme.
Statement III: Under resting physiological conditions, every \(100\text{ mL}\) of deoxygenated blood delivers approximately \(4\text{ mL}\) of \(CO_2\) to the alveoli.
Statement IV: The respiratory rhythm centre in the medulla and the pneumotaxic centre in the pons regulate respiratory rhythm, with pneumotaxic signals capable of reducing the duration of inspiration.
Statement V: The central chemosensitive area adjacent to the rhythm centre responds exclusively to blood oxygen levels, while carbon dioxide and hydrogen ions have no regulatory influence.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड परिवहन की क्रियाविधि और श्वसन के तंत्रिकीय नियमन के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित पांच कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: लगभग \(20\) से \(25\%\) \(CO_2\) का परिवहन कार्बेमीनो-हीमोग्लोबिन के रूप में तथा लगभग \(70\%\) बाइकार्बोनेट आयनों के रूप में होता है।
कथन II: लाल रक्त कणिकाओं में कार्बोनिक एनहाइड्रेज की बहुत उच्च सांद्रता पाई जाती है, जबकि रक्त प्लाज्मा में इसकी अत्यंत सूक्ष्म मात्रा होती है।
कथन III: सामान्य शारीरिक विश्राम की अवस्था में, प्रत्येक \(100\text{ mL}\) विऑक्सीकृत रक्त कूपिकाओं को लगभग \(4\text{ mL}\) \(CO_2\) प्रदान करता है।
कथन IV: मेडुला में स्थित श्वसन लय केंद्र तथा पोन्स में स्थित न्यूमोटैक्सिक केंद्र श्वसन का नियमन करते हैं, जिसमें न्यूमोटैक्सिक संकेत अंतःश्वसन की अवधि को घटा सकते हैं।
कथन V: लय केंद्र के निकट स्थित केंद्रीय रसोसंवेदी क्षेत्र केवल रक्त में ऑक्सीजन के स्तर के प्रति अनुक्रिया करता है, जबकि कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड और हाइड्रोजन आयनों का कोई प्रभाव नहीं होता।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the claim regarding carbon dioxide transport proportions
Carbon dioxide is transported in three major pools: \(20\text{ to }25\%\) bound to amine groups of globin (carbamino-haemoglobin), \(70\%\) hydrated and dissolved as bicarbonate ions (\(HCO_3^-\)), and the remaining \(7\%\) physically dissolved in plasma. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding carbonic anhydrase compartmentalization
Carbonic anhydrase is extraordinarily concentrated within erythrocytes to accelerate the reversible hydration \(\mathrm{CO}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3 \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HCO}_3^- + \mathrm{H}^+\). Blood plasma contains only minute trace amounts of this enzyme. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding carbon dioxide alveolar delivery
Every \(100\text{ mL}\) of deoxygenated blood arriving at the pulmonary alveoli delivers approximately \(4\text{ mL}\) of \(CO_2\) for exhalation, reducing venous \(CO_2\) content from \(\approx 52\text{ mL}\) to \(\approx 48\text{ mL}\) per \(100\text{ mL}\). Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding medullary and pontine centres
The medullary respiratory rhythm centre sets the baseline rhythm of inspiration. The pneumotaxic centre in the pons region sends inhibitory neural signals that truncate the duration of inspiration, thereby modulating tidal depth and accelerating respiratory frequency. Hence, this claim is accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding chemosensitive stimulation
The central chemosensitive area and peripheral arterial receptors are activated by increases in \(pCO_2\) and \([H^+]\), signaling the rhythm centre to augment ventilation and eliminate excess acid. The direct role of oxygen in regulating physiological respiratory rhythm is quite insignificant. Hence, this claim is inaccurate.

Step 6: Conclusion and Final Conceptual Answer
The transport fractions, enzymatic distribution, alveolar delivery volume, and dual medullary-pontine neural controls are all correct, while chemical regulation is mediated by carbon dioxide and hydrogen ions rather than oxygen.
Final Conceptual Answer: Only the propositions detailing carbon dioxide transport fractions, carbonic anhydrase distribution, 4 mL alveolar delivery, and medullary/pontine neural regulation are correct.

चरण 1: कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड के परिवहन अनुपातों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
लगभग \(20-25\%\) \(CO_2\) कार्बेमीनो-हीमोग्लोबिन के रूप में, \(70\%\) बाइकार्बोनेट के रूप में तथा शेष \(7\%\) प्लाज्मा में घुलकर परिवहित होती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 2: कार्बोनिक एनहाइड्रेज के वितरण संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
लाल रक्त कणिकाओं में कार्बोनिक एनहाइड्रेज प्रचुर मात्रा में होता है, जबकि रक्त प्लाज्मा में यह केवल सूक्ष्म मात्रा में पाया जाता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: कूपिकाओं को \(CO_2\) आपूर्ति संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
प्रत्येक \(100\text{ mL}\) विऑक्सीकृत रक्त कूपिकाओं को लगभग \(4\text{ mL}\) \(CO_2\) प्रदान करता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 4: मेडुला एवं पोन्स केंद्रों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
मेडुला स्थित श्वसन लय केंद्र मूल लय बनाता है और पोन्स स्थित न्यूमोटैक्सिक केंद्र अंतःश्वसन की अवधि को कम करके श्वसन दर को नियंत्रित करता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 5: रसोसंवेदी क्षेत्र की संवेदनशीलता संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
रसोसंवेदी क्षेत्र \(CO_2\) और \(H^+\) आयनों के प्रति अत्यधिक संवेदनशील होता है। श्वसन के नियमन में ऑक्सीजन की भूमिका नगण्य होती है। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 6: निष्कर्ष और अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर
प्रथम चार अवधारणाएं वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य हैं, जबकि रसोसंवेदी क्षेत्र द्वारा ऑक्सीजन की अनुक्रिया संबंधी दावा असत्य है।
अंतिम संकल्पनात्मक उत्तर: केवल प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय और चतुर्थ अवधारणाएं ही सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MATCH_Q01 - Respiratory organs across different animal groups

questiontext.text:
Match the organisms in List I with their respective respiratory structures in List II:

List I (Organisms)List II (Respiratory Structures)
(A) Earthworm(I) Network of tracheal tubes
(B) Aquatic arthropods(II) Entire body surface
(C) Lower invertebrates (Sponges)(III) Moist cuticle
(D) Insects(IV) Gills

Select the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the respiratory structures of lower invertebrates.
Lower invertebrates such as sponges, coelenterates, and flatworms exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide by simple diffusion across their entire body surface.

Step 2: Analyze the respiratory mechanism of earthworms.
Earthworms utilize their moist cuticle for cutaneous exchange of respiratory gases.

Step 3: Analyze the respiratory mechanism of aquatic arthropods.
Aquatic arthropods, such as prawns, possess specialized vascularized structures called gills (branchial respiration) for gaseous exchange.

Step 4: Analyze the respiratory mechanism of insects.
Insects utilize an extensive network of tracheal tubes that conduct atmospheric air directly to body tissues.

Step 5: Formulate the matching pairs and final answer.
Earthworm pairs with Moist cuticle (A-III); Aquatic arthropods pair with Gills (B-IV); Lower invertebrates pair with Entire body surface (C-II); Insects pair with Network of tracheal tubes (D-I). The correct combination is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

answer.text: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MATCH_Q02 - Standard respiratory lung volumes

questiontext.text:
Match the respiratory volumes listed in List I with their typical physiological values in List II:

List I (Respiratory Volume)List II (Typical Volume)
(A) Tidal Volume (TV)(I) \(1000\text{ mL to }1100\text{ mL}\)
(B) Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV)(II) \(1100\text{ mL to }1200\text{ mL}\)
(C) Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV)(III) \(500\text{ mL}\)
(D) Residual Volume (RV)(IV) \(2500\text{ mL to }3000\text{ mL}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify Tidal Volume (TV).
Tidal volume is the volume of air inspired or expired during a normal respiration, which is approximately \(500\text{ mL}\).

Step 2: Identify Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV).
IRV is the additional volume of air a person can inspire by a forcible inspiration, averaging \(2500\text{ mL to }3000\text{ mL}\).

Step 3: Identify Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV).
ERV is the additional volume of air a person can expire by a forcible expiration, averaging \(1000\text{ mL to }1100\text{ mL}\).

Step 4: Identify Residual Volume (RV).
RV is the volume of air remaining in the lungs even after a forcible expiration, averaging \(1100\text{ mL to }1200\text{ mL}\).

Step 5: Correlate the pairs to determine the final match.
The correct association is Tidal Volume with \(500\text{ mL}\) (A-III), Inspiratory Reserve Volume with \(2500\text{ mL to }3000\text{ mL}\) (B-IV), Expiratory Reserve Volume with \(1000\text{ mL to }1100\text{ mL}\) (C-I), and Residual Volume with \(1100\text{ mL to }1200\text{ mL}\) (D-II). The correct sequence is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

answer.text: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MATCH_Q03 - Pulmonary capacities and derived volume combinations

questiontext.text:
Match the pulmonary capacities in List I with their corresponding constituent volumes in List II:

List I (Pulmonary Capacity)List II (Constituent Volumes)
(A) Inspiratory Capacity (IC)(I) \(\text{ERV} + \text{RV}\)
(B) Expiratory Capacity (EC)(II) \(\text{ERV} + \text{TV} + \text{IRV}\)
(C) Functional Residual Capacity (FRC)(III) \(\text{TV} + \text{IRV}\)
(D) Vital Capacity (VC)(IV) \(\text{TV} + \text{ERV}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define Inspiratory Capacity.
Inspiratory capacity is the total volume of air a person can inspire after a normal expiration; it includes Tidal Volume and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (\(\text{TV} + \text{IRV}\)).

Step 2: Define Expiratory Capacity.
Expiratory capacity is the total volume of air a person can expire after a normal inspiration; it includes Tidal Volume and Expiratory Reserve Volume (\(\text{TV} + \text{ERV}\)).

Step 3: Define Functional Residual Capacity.
Functional residual capacity is the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal expiration; it consists of Expiratory Reserve Volume and Residual Volume (\(\text{ERV} + \text{RV}\)).

Step 4: Define Vital Capacity.
Vital capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration (or breathe out after a forced inspiration); it encompasses \(\text{ERV} + \text{TV} + \text{IRV}\).

Step 5: Identify the final matched combination.

Step 2: Correlate the anatomy of the trachea.
The trachea is a straight tube extending through the mid-thoracic cavity that divides at the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra into right and left primary bronchi.

Step 3: Correlate the role of pleural fluid.

questiontext.text:

List I (Regulatory Element)List II (Location and Function)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role of the respiratory rhythm centre.
The respiratory rhythm centre is a specialized neural group located in the medulla oblongata that is primarily responsible for generating and maintaining the basal rhythm of respiration.

Step 2: Identify the role of the pneumotaxic centre.
The pneumotaxic centre is situated in the pons varolii; signals from this centre can reduce the duration of inspiration, thereby modulating the respiratory rate.

Step 3: Identify the role of the central chemosensitive area.
The central chemosensitive area lies adjacent to the rhythm centre in the medulla and is highly sensitive to increases in \(\text{CO}_2\) and hydrogen ion (\(\text{H}^+\)) concentrations.

Step 4: Identify the role of peripheral vascular receptors.
Receptors present in the aortic arch and carotid bodies detect arterial elevations in \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}^+\) concentrations and relay corrective signals to the medulla rhythm centre.

Step 5: Compile the correct pairing sequence.
Respiratory rhythm centre pairs with Medulla centre responsible for rhythm (A-III); Pneumotaxic centre pairs with Pons centre altering inspiration duration (B-I); Central chemosensitive area pairs with Medulla region activated by \(\text{CO}_2\) and \(\text{H}^+\) (C-IV); Aortic and carotid receptors pair with Peripheral chemoreceptors (D-II). Step 1: Understand the clinical pathology of asthma.
Asthma is characterized by wheezing and dyspnea due to allergic inflammation and bronchospasm of the bronchi and bronchioles.

Step 2: Understand the pathological mechanism of emphysema.
Emphysema is a chronic pulmonary disease, primarily caused by cigarette smoking, wherein the alveolar septa/walls are damaged, permanently reducing the total surface area available for gas exchange.

Step 3: Understand occupational fibrosis.
Occupational respiratory disorders arise in industries involving grinding or stone-breaking where chronic dust exposure overstimulates fibrous tissue proliferation (fibrosis), causing severe lung damage.

Step 4: Understand cutaneous respiration.
Cutaneous respiration is gas exchange occurring directly across vascularized, moist integument/skin, commonly observed in amphibians such as frogs.

Step 5: Determine the matching sequence.
Asthma pairs with Inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles (A-II); Emphysema pairs with Damage to alveolar walls decreasing respiratory surface (B-III); Fibrosis pairs with Proliferation of fibrous tissue from chronic dust exposure (C-I); Cutaneous respiration pairs with Exchange across moist skin (D-IV). name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MATCH_Q09 - Quantitative transport forms of respiratory gases in blood

Step 1: Evaluate the fractions of oxygen transport.
About \(97\%\) of oxygen is transported bound to haemoglobin inside red blood cells as oxyhaemoglobin, whereas the remaining \(3\%\) is carried dissolved in blood plasma.

Step 2: Evaluate the major form of carbon dioxide transport.
Nearly \(70\%\) of carbon dioxide is transported in blood in the form of bicarbonate ions (\(\text{HCO}_3^-\)), facilitated by the enzyme carbonic anhydrase.

Step 3: Evaluate carbamino-haemoglobin transport.
Nearly \(20\text{ to }25\%\) of carbon dioxide is transported bound to the amine groups of haemoglobin as carbamino-haemoglobin.

Step 4: Evaluate dissolved carbon dioxide in plasma.
About \(7\%\) of carbon dioxide is carried in a simple dissolved physical state within blood plasma.

Step 5: Deduce the matching sequence.
Oxygen by RBCs pairs with \(97\%\) (A-III); Carbon dioxide as bicarbonate pairs with \(70\%\) (B-I); Carbon dioxide as carbamino-haemoglobin pairs with \(20\text{ to }25\%\) (C-II); Carbon dioxide dissolved in plasma pairs with \(7\%\) (D-IV). name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MATCH_Q10 - Physiological factors governing haemoglobin oxygenation and delivery

questiontext.text:
Match the physiological parameters and delivery values in List I with their respective physiological states or values in List II:

List I (Physiological Condition / Process)List II (Characteristic / Quantitative Value)
(A) Conditions at alveolar surface favourable for oxyhaemoglobin formation(I) High \(\text{pCO}_2\), low \(\text{pO}_2\), high \(\text{H}^+\), higher temperature
(B) Conditions in active peripheral tissues causing oxygen dissociation(II) High \(\text{pO}_2\), low \(\text{pCO}_2\), lesser \(\text{H}^+\), lower temperature
(C) Volume of \(\text{O}_2\) delivered to tissues by \(100\text{ mL}\) oxygenated blood(III) Approximately \(4\text{ mL}\)
(D) Volume of \(\text{CO}_2\) delivered to alveoli by \(100\text{ mL}\) deoxygenated blood(IV) Approximately \(5\text{ mL}\)

Choose the correct matching arrangement from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze conditions favouring oxyhaemoglobin synthesis.
In the alveoli, the presence of high partial pressure of oxygen (\(\text{pO}_2\)), low partial pressure of carbon dioxide (\(\text{pCO}_2\)), lower hydrogen ion concentration (higher pH), and lower temperature shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the left and promotes oxyhaemoglobin formation.

Step 2: Analyze conditions favouring oxygen dissociation at tissues.
In active metabolizing body tissues, low \(\text{pO}_2\), elevated \(\text{pCO}_2\), high \(\text{H}^+\) ion concentration, and higher temperature facilitate the release and dissociation of oxygen from oxyhaemoglobin.

Step 3: Quantify oxygen delivery to tissues.
Under resting physiological conditions, every \(100\text{ mL}\) of oxygenated systemic arterial blood delivers approximately \(5\text{ mL}\) of oxygen to the tissues.

Step 4: Quantify carbon dioxide delivery to alveoli.
Every \(100\text{ mL}\) of deoxygenated blood returning to pulmonary circulation delivers approximately \(4\text{ mL}\) of carbon dioxide to the alveoli for expiration.

Step 5: Conclude the final match.
Conditions at alveolar surface match with High \(\text{pO}_2\), low \(\text{pCO}_2\), lesser \(\text{H}^+\), lower temperature (A-II); Conditions in tissues match with High \(\text{pCO}_2\), low \(\text{pO}_2\), high \(\text{H}^+\), higher temperature (B-I); Oxygen delivered per \(100\text{ mL}\) matches with \(5\text{ mL}\) (C-IV); Carbon dioxide delivered per \(100\text{ mL}\) matches with \(4\text{ mL}\) (D-III). name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER14_MCQ_Q01 - Sequence of events occurring during inspiration

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following physiological events of normal human inspiration in the correct chronological sequence:

I. Expansion of the thoracic chamber volume
II. Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles
III. Inflow of atmospheric air into the lungs
IV. Increase in pulmonary volume
V. Fall in intra-pulmonary pressure below atmospheric pressure

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Inspiration is an active process governed by Boyle's law and pressure gradients between the atmosphere and the intra-pulmonary cavity. Air flows from an area of higher pressure to an area of lower pressure.

Step 2: Sequential Analysis of Events
1. Inspiration is initiated by the contraction of the diaphragm (which moves downward, increasing the thoracic volume along the antero-posterior axis) and the contraction of the external intercostal muscles (which lifts the ribs and sternum, increasing the thoracic volume along the dorso-ventral axis).
2. These muscle contractions lead directly to an overall increase in the volume of the thoracic chamber.
3. Because the lungs are held closely against the thoracic wall by pleural fluid and negative intrapleural pressure, the enlargement of the thoracic cavity results in an identical expansion of the pulmonary volume.
4. An increase in pulmonary volume causes the intra-pulmonary pressure to drop slightly below atmospheric pressure (creating a negative pressure gradient).
5. Due to this generated negative pressure gradient, atmospheric air rushes from the exterior through the respiratory tract into the alveoli until equilibrium is reached.

Step 3: Verification of the Sequence
The chronological order of events is therefore: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles (II) → Expansion of the thoracic chamber volume (I) → Increase in pulmonary volume (IV) → Fall in intra-pulmonary pressure below atmospheric pressure (V) → Inflow of atmospheric air into the lungs (III).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct logical sequence is II → I → IV → V → III.

answer.text: II → I → IV → V → III
I → II → IV → V → III
II → IV → I → III → V
I → IV → II → V → III

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER14_MCQ_Q02 - Correct anatomical sequence of human respiratory tract

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following anatomical structures in the correct sequence through which inspired atmospheric air travels from the external environment to the actual site of gas exchange:

I. Larynx
II. Pharynx
III. Terminal bronchioles
IV. Trachea
V. Alveoli
VI. Primary bronchi

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human respiratory system is structurally divided into a conducting zone and a respiratory (exchange) zone. Inhaled air travels progressively through a branched anatomical passage from the external environment down to the functional diffusion units.

Step 2: Sequential Analysis of Pathway
1. Atmospheric air enters through a pair of external nostrils into the nasal chamber.
2. The nasal chamber opens into the pharynx, which serves as the common passage for both food and air.
3. The pharynx opens through the glottis into the larynx (the cartilaginous sound box).
4. From the larynx, air moves into the trachea, a straight tube extending down to the mid-thoracic cavity.
5. At the level of the 5th thoracic vertebra, the trachea divides into the right and left primary bronchi.
6. Each primary bronchus undergoes repeated divisions into secondary and tertiary bronchi, followed by branching bronchioles, terminating in very thin terminal bronchioles.
7. Finally, each terminal bronchiole opens into the alveolar ducts and bag-like alveoli, where actual gaseous exchange takes place.

Step 3: Verification of the Sequence
Tracing the given structures in order from outside inward: Pharynx (II) → Larynx (I) → Trachea (IV) → Primary bronchi (VI) → Terminal bronchioles (III) → Alveoli (V).

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct anatomical sequence is II → I → IV → VI → III → V.

answer.text: II → I → IV → VI → III → V
II → IV → I → VI → III → V
I → II → IV → III → VI → V
II → I → VI → IV → III → V

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the mechanics of resting expiration.
Under resting conditions, expiration does not require active muscular contraction.

Step 2: Identify the muscle states.
Relaxation of both the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles returns the ribs, sternum, and diaphragm to their resting positions, decreasing pulmonary volume.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Quiet expiration results from the relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles.

answer.text: Relaxation of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles
Contraction of internal intercostal and abdominal muscles
Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals
Relaxation of abdominal muscles alone

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q12 - Muscles recruited for forceful breathing

questiontext.text: To enhance the strength and depth of expiration during forceful breathing, humans recruit additional muscles located in the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand forced breathing mechanics.
Normal quiet expiration is passive, but forceful expiration requires active muscular compression.

Step 2: Identify the accessory muscular groups.
Additional muscles present in the abdomen (and internal intercostals) contract to push the diaphragm upward and pull ribs downward.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Additional muscles in the abdomen are recruited to increase expiratory force.

answer.text: Abdomen
Larynx
Pericardium
Vertebral column

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q13 - Typical resting respiratory frequency

questiontext.text: Under resting conditions, an average healthy adult human breathes at a rate of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the standard physiological breathing rate in healthy humans.
Under basal resting conditions, respiratory rhythm centre drives regular cyclical ventilation.

Step 2: State the textbook range.
The average respiratory rate is 12 to 16 breaths per minute.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The physiological breathing rate is 12–16 times/minute.

answer.text: 12–16 times/minute
20–25 times/minute
70–75 times/minute
4–8 times/minute

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q14 - Total hourly ventilation from tidal volume

questiontext.text: If a healthy individual has a resting tidal volume of \(500\text{ mL}\) and breathes \(14\text{ times per minute}\), what is the total volume of air inspired in one hour?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Calculate minute respiratory volume.
\(\text{Minute volume} = \text{Tidal Volume} \times \text{Breaths per minute} = 500\text{ mL} \times 14 = 7000\text{ mL/min} = 7\text{ L/min}\).

Step 2: Convert minute ventilation into hourly ventilation.
\(\text{Hourly volume} = 7000\text{ mL/min} \times 60\text{ min} = 420{,}000\text{ mL} = 420\text{ L}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The total air volume inspired in one hour equals \(420\text{ L}\) (or \(420{,}000\text{ mL}\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q15 - Typical range for inspiratory reserve volume

questiontext.text: The additional volume of air that a healthy human can inspire by a forcible inspiration (Inspiratory Reserve Volume, IRV) averages:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV).
IRV is the extra volume of air an individual can inhale beyond normal tidal inspiration.

Step 2: Recall standard clinical physiological values.
The average range given in standard human physiology is \(2500\text{ mL}\) to \(3000\text{ mL}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The average IRV is \(2500\text{ mL}\) to \(3000\text{ mL}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q16 - Residual volume definition and value

questiontext.text: The volume of air that remains inside the lungs even after the most strenuous, forcible expiration is termed:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define the volume of gas that cannot be exhaled.
Lungs never collapse entirely during breathing; a cushion of gas is retained inside the alveoli and airways.

Step 2: Match with standard terminology.
This volume is called Residual Volume (RV) and averages \(1100\text{ mL}\) to \(1200\text{ mL}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The air remaining after forcible expiration is Residual Volume.

answer.text: Residual Volume (RV)
Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV)
Tidal Volume (TV)
Functional Residual Capacity (FRC)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q17 - Calculation of inspiratory capacity

questiontext.text: A spirometry test shows a person's Tidal Volume (\(\mathrm{TV}\)) is \(500\text{ mL}\) and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (\(\mathrm{IRV}\)) is \(2800\text{ mL}\). What is this individual's Inspiratory Capacity (\(\mathrm{IC}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the definition and formula for Inspiratory Capacity.
Inspiratory Capacity is the total volume of air a person can inhale after a normal expiration: \(\mathrm{IC} = \mathrm{TV} + \mathrm{IRV}\).

Step 2: Substitute the given clinical values.
\(\mathrm{IC} = 500\text{ mL} + 2800\text{ mL} = 3300\text{ mL}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The Inspiratory Capacity is \(3300\text{ mL}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q18 - Formulation of functional residual capacity

questiontext.text: Functional Residual Capacity (\(\mathrm{FRC}\)) represents the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal expiration and is mathematically equal to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the state of the lungs following normal quiet expiration.
After a normal expiration, the lungs still contain the air that could be voluntarily pushed out plus the air that cannot be exhaled at all.

Step 2: Combine the relevant respiratory volumes.
The volume remaining is Expiratory Reserve Volume (\(\mathrm{ERV}\)) plus Residual Volume (\(\mathrm{RV}\)), so \(\mathrm{FRC} = \mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{RV}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Functional Residual Capacity equals \(\mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{RV}\).

answer.text: \(\mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{RV}\)
\(\mathrm{TV} + \mathrm{RV}\)
\(\mathrm{IRV} + \mathrm{ERV}\)
\(\mathrm{VC} - \mathrm{ERV}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q19 - Definition and components of vital capacity

questiontext.text: Vital Capacity (\(\mathrm{VC}\)) of the human lung is correctly represented by which combination of respiratory volumes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define Vital Capacity.
Vital Capacity is the maximum volume of air a person can breathe in after a forced expiration (or breathe out after a forced inspiration).

Step 2: Identify the components.
It comprises Expiratory Reserve Volume (\(\mathrm{ERV}\)), Tidal Volume (\(\mathrm{TV}\)), and Inspiratory Reserve Volume (\(\mathrm{IRV}\)).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Vital Capacity is \(\mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{TV} + \mathrm{IRV}\).

answer.text: \(\mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{TV} + \mathrm{IRV}\)
\(\mathrm{TV} + \mathrm{IRV} + \mathrm{RV}\)
\(\mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{TV} + \mathrm{RV}\)
\(\mathrm{TLC} - \mathrm{IRV}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q20 - Spirometric measurement limits in diagnosis

questiontext.text: Which pulmonary volume or capacity CANNOT be measured directly using a standard spirometer?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the mechanism of spirometry.
A spirometer measures the volume of air moved into and out of the respiratory tract during breathing movements.

Step 2: Identify volumes that cannot be moved into the spirometer.
Residual Volume (\(\mathrm{RV}\)) cannot be exhaled under any circumstance. Consequently, any capacity containing \(\mathrm{RV}\)—such as Functional Residual Capacity (\(\mathrm{FRC}\)) and Total Lung Capacity (\(\mathrm{TLC}\))—cannot be measured directly with a spirometer.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Residual Volume cannot be measured directly using a spirometer.

answer.text: Residual Volume (\(\mathrm{RV}\))
Tidal Volume (\(\mathrm{TV}\))
Inspiratory Reserve Volume (\(\mathrm{IRV}\))
Vital Capacity (\(\mathrm{VC}\))

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q21 - Derivation of total lung capacity

questiontext.text: If a person has a Vital Capacity of \(4600\text{ mL}\) and a Functional Residual Capacity of \(2300\text{ mL}\), with an Expiratory Reserve Volume of \(1100\text{ mL}\), what is their Total Lung Capacity (\(\mathrm{TLC}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Calculate Residual Volume (\(\mathrm{RV}\)) from Functional Residual Capacity.
\(\mathrm{FRC} = \mathrm{ERV} + \mathrm{RV} \implies \mathrm{RV} = \mathrm{FRC} - \mathrm{ERV} = 2300\text{ mL} - 1100\text{ mL} = 1200\text{ mL}\).

Step 2: Compute Total Lung Capacity (\(\mathrm{TLC}\)).
\(\mathrm{TLC} = \mathrm{VC} + \mathrm{RV} = 4600\text{ mL} + 1200\text{ mL} = 5800\text{ mL}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The Total Lung Capacity is \(5800\text{ mL}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q22 - Oxygen partial pressure in alveolar air

questiontext.text: What are the partial pressures of oxygen (\(p\mathrm{O_2}\)) and carbon dioxide (\(p\mathrm{CO_2}\)) respectively in alveolar air under standard physiological conditions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review alveolar gas partial pressures.
In alveolar air, constant gas exchange with pulmonary blood lowers \(p\mathrm{O_2}\) and raises \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\) compared to ambient air.

Step 2: State the standard values from Table 14.1.
Alveolar air has a \(p\mathrm{O_2}\) of \(104\text{ mm Hg}\) and a \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\) of \(40\text{ mm Hg}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The partial pressures are \(104\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(40\text{ mm Hg}\) respectively.

answer.text: \(104\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(40\text{ mm Hg}\)
\(159\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(0.3\text{ mm Hg}\)
\(40\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(45\text{ mm Hg}\)
\(95\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(40\text{ mm Hg}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q23 - Partial pressure values in deoxygenated blood

questiontext.text: In systemic venous (deoxygenated) blood entering the pulmonary circulation, the values of \(p\mathrm{O_2}\) and \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\) are:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze gas partial pressures in systemic venous blood.
Deoxygenated blood returns from metabolically active tissues where oxygen is extracted and carbon dioxide is added.

Step 2: Recall textbook values.
In deoxygenated blood, \(p\mathrm{O_2}\) is \(40\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\) is \(45\text{ mm Hg}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The values are \(p\mathrm{O_2} = 40\text{ mm Hg}\) and \(p\mathrm{CO_2} = 45\text{ mm Hg}\).

answer.text: \(p\mathrm{O_2} = 40\text{ mm Hg}\), \(p\mathrm{CO_2} = 45\text{ mm Hg}\)
\(p\mathrm{O_2} = 95\text{ mm Hg}\), \(p\mathrm{CO_2} = 40\text{ mm Hg}\)
\(p\mathrm{O_2} = 104\text{ mm Hg}\), \(p\mathrm{CO_2} = 40\text{ mm Hg}\)
\(p\mathrm{O_2} = 45\text{ mm Hg}\), \(p\mathrm{CO_2} = 40\text{ mm Hg}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q24 - Carbon dioxide solubility and diffusion rate

questiontext.text: The solubility of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) in blood and tissue fluids is how many times higher than that of \(\mathrm{O_2}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the solubility factor affecting gas diffusion.
Diffusion rate is directly proportional to gas solubility through the respiratory membrane.

Step 2: Recall the exact comparative solubility ratio.
The solubility of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is 20 to 25 times higher than that of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The solubility of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is 20–25 times higher than that of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

answer.text: 20–25 times
2–5 times
10–15 times

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q25 - Layers of the alveolar diffusion membrane

questiontext.text: The diffusion membrane across which respiratory gas exchange occurs consists of which three microscopic layers?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the anatomical barriers separating alveolar air from capillary blood.
Gases must cross the alveolar wall, an intervening extracellular matrix, and the blood vessel wall.

Step 2: Name the specific histological layers.
These are: (1) thin squamous epithelium of the alveoli, (2) endothelium of alveolar capillaries, and (3) the intervening basement substance supporting both cellular layers.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The three layers are squamous epithelium of alveoli, capillary endothelium, and the basement substance between them.

answer.text: Squamous epithelium of alveoli, endothelium of alveolar capillaries, and basement substance between them
Ciliated columnar epithelium, smooth muscle layer, and capillary endothelium
Cuboidal epithelium of alveoli, tunica media, and capillary basement membrane
Pseudostratified epithelium, pleural fluid layer, and endothelial lining

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q26 - Total thickness of the diffusion membrane

questiontext.text: The total thickness of the human alveolar-capillary diffusion membrane is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the structural adaptation for efficient diffusion.
Fick's law of diffusion dictates that the rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to membrane thickness.

Step 2: Recall the textbook dimension.
The combined thickness of all three layers of the diffusion membrane is much less than a millimetre (\(\ll 1\text{ mm}\), roughly \(0.2\text{ to }0.5\ \mu\mathrm{m}\)).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The thickness is much less than a millimetre.

answer.text: Much less than a millimetre
Between \(2\text{ mm}\) and \(3\text{ mm}\)
Exactly \(1\text{ cm}\)
Around \(5\text{ mm}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q27 - Proportions of oxygen transport forms

questiontext.text: In human blood, oxygen is transported in two forms. The respective percentages transported by red blood cells and dissolved in plasma are:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify oxygen transport mechanisms in blood.
Oxygen has low solubility in aqueous solutions, requiring a chemical carrier.

Step 2: Quantify the two modes.
About 97 percent of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) is transported bound to haemoglobin in RBCs, while the remaining 3 percent is carried in a dissolved state through plasma.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The percentages are 97% by RBCs and 3% dissolved in plasma.

answer.text: 97% by RBCs and 3% dissolved in plasma
70% by RBCs and 30% dissolved in plasma
80% by RBCs and 20% dissolved in plasma
50% by RBCs and 50% dissolved in plasma

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q28 - Forms and percentages of carbon dioxide transport

questiontext.text: Which option correctly details the percentages of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) transported as bicarbonate, carbamino-haemoglobin, and in dissolved state through plasma?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify all three modes of carbon dioxide transport.
Carbon dioxide is carried as bicarbonate ions (\(\mathrm{HCO_3^-}\)), bound to amine groups of haemoglobin, and dissolved directly in plasma.

Step 2: Recall textbook percentages for each mode.
Bicarbonate accounts for about 70%, carbamino-haemoglobin accounts for 20–25%, and dissolved state in plasma accounts for about 7%.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The correct values are 70% as bicarbonate, 20–25% as carbamino-haemoglobin, and 7% dissolved in plasma.

answer.text: 70% as bicarbonate, 20–25% as carbamino-haemoglobin, 7% dissolved in plasma
97% as bicarbonate, 3% as carbamino-haemoglobin, 0% dissolved in plasma
20–25% as bicarbonate, 70% as carbamino-haemoglobin, 7% dissolved in plasma
50% as bicarbonate, 40% as carbamino-haemoglobin, 10% dissolved in plasma

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q29 - Stoichiometry of haemoglobin oxygen binding

questiontext.text: Each molecule of human haemoglobin possesses four iron-containing haeme groups and can bind reversibly with a maximum of how many molecules of \(\mathrm{O_2}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the quaternary structure of haemoglobin.
Haemoglobin is a tetramer consisting of four globin subunits, each containing one ferrous (\(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\)) haeme moiety.

Step 2: Relate binding capacity to haeme groups.
Each haeme group binds one diatomic oxygen molecule (\(\mathrm{O_2}\)), allowing a single haemoglobin molecule to carry up to four molecules of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Haemoglobin can carry a maximum of four molecules of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

answer.text: Four molecules of \(\mathrm{O_2}\)
Two molecules of \(\mathrm{O_2}\)
Eight molecules of \(\mathrm{O_2}\)
One molecule of \(\mathrm{O_2}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q30 - Conditions favouring oxyhaemoglobin formation in alveoli

questiontext.text: Which set of physiological conditions at the alveolar surface favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify factors affecting haemoglobin-oxygen affinity.
Oxygen loading is favoured by high substrate availability and conditions that stabilize the relaxed (R) state of haemoglobin.

Step 2: Evaluate alveolar conditions.
In pulmonary alveoli, there is high \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), low \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), low \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration (higher pH), and lower temperature.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
High \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), low \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), lesser \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and lower temperature favour oxyhaemoglobin formation.

answer.text: High \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), low \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), lesser \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and lower temperature
Low \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), high \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), high \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and higher temperature
High \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), high \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), high \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and lower temperature
Low \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), low \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), lesser \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and higher temperature

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q31 - Factors promoting oxygen unloading at tissues

questiontext.text: At the level of metabolically active peripheral tissues, oxygen dissociates from oxyhaemoglobin primarily because of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine peripheral tissue microenvironment.
Cellular respiration consumes oxygen and generates carbon dioxide, heat, and metabolic acids.

Step 2: Relate microenvironment to haemoglobin affinity.
Low \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), high \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), high \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and elevated temperature decrease haemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, promoting dissociation.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Low \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), high \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), high \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and higher temperature drive oxygen dissociation.

answer.text: Low \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), high \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), high \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and higher temperature
High \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), low \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), low \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and lower temperature
High \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), high \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), low \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and higher temperature
Low \(p\mathrm{O_2}\), low \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\), low \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration, and lower temperature

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q32 - Shape of the oxygen haemoglobin dissociation curve

questiontext.text: When the percentage saturation of haemoglobin with \(\mathrm{O_2}\) is plotted against the partial pressure of oxygen (\(p\mathrm{O_2}\)), the resulting curve exhibits a:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand haemoglobin allosteric cooperative binding.
Binding of the first oxygen molecule increases the affinity of the remaining haeme subunits for oxygen.

Step 2: Identify the mathematical curve shape.
This cooperative binding mechanism generates a characteristic S-shaped or sigmoid curve.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
A sigmoid curve is obtained.

answer.text: Sigmoid curve
Hyperbolic curve
Linear straight line
Parabolic curve

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q33 - Oxygen delivery per 100 mL blood

questiontext.text: Under normal resting physiological conditions, every \(100\text{ mL}\) of oxygenated blood delivers approximately how much \(\mathrm{O_2}\) to the tissues?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine oxygen content of systemic blood.
\(100\text{ mL}\) of fully oxygenated blood carries approximately \(19.4\text{ to }20\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

Step 2: Determine tissue extraction under resting conditions.
Venous blood leaving resting tissues remains roughly 75% saturated, carrying about \(14\text{ to }15\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) per \(100\text{ mL}\).

Step 3: Calculate the delivered volume.
The net quantity delivered to tissues is approximately \(5\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) per \(100\text{ mL}\) of blood.

Step 4: State the final conclusion.
Every \(100\text{ mL}\) of oxygenated blood delivers approximately \(5\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q34 - Carbon dioxide delivery to alveoli

questiontext.text: Under normal resting conditions, every \(100\text{ mL}\) of deoxygenated blood delivers approximately how much \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) to the pulmonary alveoli?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand carbon dioxide transport and unloading.
Deoxygenated blood carries carbon dioxide collected from active tissues back to the lungs.

Step 2: Recall the physiological delivery value.
Under resting conditions, every \(100\text{ mL}\) of deoxygenated blood delivers approximately \(4\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) into the alveoli.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The volume delivered is approximately \(4\text{ mL}\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q35 - Carbonic anhydrase localization and activity

questiontext.text: The zinc-containing metalloenzyme carbonic anhydrase facilitates the reversible conversion of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) into carbonic acid. This enzyme is found in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the cellular distribution of carbonic anhydrase in blood.
Red blood cells require extremely rapid interconversion of dissolved \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and bicarbonate ions during transit through capillaries.

Step 2: Contrast RBC concentration with plasma.
RBCs contain a very high concentration of carbonic anhydrase, whereas plasma contains only minute quantities of the enzyme.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Very high concentration is present in RBCs, with minute quantities in plasma.

answer.text: Very high concentrations in RBCs and minute quantities in plasma
High concentrations in plasma and completely absent in RBCs
Equal concentrations in RBCs and plasma
Platelets only, being absent in both RBCs and plasma

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q36 - Primary neural centre governing respiratory rhythm

questiontext.text: The primary specialised neural centre primarily responsible for maintaining and regulating the basic respiratory rhythm in humans is located in the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify brainstem centres controlling ventilation.
The brainstem contains rhythm generators and regulatory modulating centres.

Step 2: Distinguish the primary rhythm generator.
The respiratory rhythm centre is located in the medulla oblongata and is primarily responsible for basic cyclical breathing movements.

Step 3: Contrast with the pons.
The pneumotaxic centre in the pons modulates the rhythm centre rather than generating the primary rhythm.

Step 4: State the final conclusion.
The primary centre is situated in the medulla region of the brain.

answer.text: Medulla oblongata
Pons
Cerebellum
Cerebrum

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q37 - Pneumotaxic centre location and function

questiontext.text: The pneumotaxic centre is situated in the pons region of the brain. Its primary regulatory action on the respiratory rhythm centre is to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the modulatory role of the pneumotaxic centre.
Neural signals transmitted from the pneumotaxic centre switch off inspiration.

Step 2: Determine the effect on respiratory rate.
By reducing the duration of inspiration, it prevents lung over-inflation and increases the respiratory frequency.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Signals from the pneumotaxic centre reduce the duration of inspiration and thereby alter respiratory rate.

answer.text: Reduce the duration of inspiration and alter the respiratory rate
Prolong the duration of inspiration and cause hypoventilation
Directly monitor oxygen concentration in the arterial blood
Stimulate relaxation of abdominal muscles during forced expiration

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q38 - Chemical sensitivity of central chemoreceptors

questiontext.text: The chemosensitive area situated adjacent to the medullary respiratory rhythm centre is highly sensitive to increases in which chemical species?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify chemical stimuli for central respiratory control.
The central chemosensitive area detects changes in cerebrospinal fluid and surrounding interstitial fluid chemistry.

Step 2: Recall specific chemical triggers.
It responds with high sensitivity to elevated \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and hydrogen ions (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)), signaling the rhythm centre to stimulate ventilation.

Step 3: Contrast with oxygen sensitivity.
The role of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) in the direct regulation of respiratory rhythm is considered insignificant.

Step 4: State the final conclusion.
The chemosensitive area is sensitive to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and hydrogen ions.

answer.text: \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and hydrogen ions (\(\mathrm{H^+}\))
Dissolved \(\mathrm{O_2}\) only
Nitrogen gas and glucose
Bicarbonate ions and sodium ions

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q39 - Insignificant role of oxygen in rhythm regulation

questiontext.text: In the physiological regulation of resting respiratory rhythm in humans, the direct sensory role of which factor is considered quite insignificant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate relative roles of blood gases in respiratory drive.
Ventilatory drive is dominated by feedback from central and peripheral chemoreceptors responding to hypercapnia (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\)) and acidosis (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)).

Step 2: Note the textbook assertion on oxygen.
The role of oxygen in regulating normal respiratory rhythm is quite insignificant.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Oxygen plays an insignificant role in regulating respiratory rhythm.

answer.text: Oxygen (\(\mathrm{O_2}\))
Carbon dioxide (\(\mathrm{CO_2}\))
Hydrogen ion concentration (\(\mathrm{H^+}\))
Arterial \(p\mathrm{CO_2}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q40 - Peripheral arterial chemoreceptors

questiontext.text: Peripheral chemoreceptors capable of recognizing changes in arterial \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{H^+}\) concentration to modulate respiratory output are located in the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify arterial vascular structures housing chemosensory bodies.
Receptors monitoring circulating blood composition are located at strategic major arterial sites.

Step 2: Recall the specific anatomical locations.
Sensory receptors associated with the aortic arch and carotid artery detect elevations in \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{H^+}\) and transmit afferent signals to the respiratory rhythm centre.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Receptors are located in the aortic arch and carotid artery.

answer.text: Aortic arch and carotid artery
Pulmonary vein and superior vena cava
Coronary sinus and renal artery
Hepatic portal vein and pulmonary artery

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q41 - Underlying pathology of asthma

questiontext.text: Asthma is a respiratory disorder characterized clinically by wheezing and difficulty in breathing due to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the primary pathophysiology of asthma.
Asthma involves hypersensitivity of the lower airways.

Step 2: Connect pathology to clinical symptoms.
Inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles causes airway narrowing, spasms, and wheezing during breathing.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The symptom complex is caused by inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles.

answer.text: Inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles
Destruction and damage of alveolar walls
Fibrous proliferation in the upper nasal mucosa
Loss of surfactant in terminal alveolar ducts

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q42 - Pathological hallmark of pulmonary emphysema

questiontext.text: A chronic respiratory disorder often caused by cigarette smoking in which the alveolar walls are damaged and the respiratory surface is significantly decreased is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify chronic obstructive pathology linked to smoking.
Chronic exposure to cigarette smoke irritates alveolar septa and triggers enzymatic breakdown of elastic fibres.

Step 2: Match damage pattern to disease name.
The destruction of alveolar walls resulting in reduced gas exchange surface area is diagnostic of emphysema.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
The disorder described is emphysema.

answer.text: Emphysema
Asthma
Silicosis
Pleurisy

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BREATHINGANDEXCHANGEOFGASES_MCQ_Q43 - Chronic stone dust exposure and fibrosis

questiontext.text: In occupational respiratory disorders associated with stone-breaking and grinding industries, chronic dust inhalation leads to lung damage primarily through:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the physiological effect of prolonged mineral dust inhalation.
Excess silica or mineral dust overwhelms alveolar macrophage defense mechanisms.

Step 2: Identify the histological outcome.
Persistent irritation triggers chronic inflammation leading to fibrosis (proliferation of fibrous connective tissue) and irreversible loss of lung elasticity.

Step 3: State the final conclusion.
Damage occurs via chronic inflammation leading to fibrosis (proliferation of fibrous tissues).

answer.text: Chronic inflammation leading to fibrosis (proliferation of fibrous tissues)
Acute bacterial infection of tracheal cartilaginous rings
Excessive accumulation of pleural fluid causing pleural friction
